item.title: [News] Asymmetry: 2027 Assistant Curator Fellowship Nottingham Contemporary (UK)
item.description:
Asymmetry have announced a global Open Call for the inaugural Asymmetry Assistant Curator Fellowship at Nottingham Contemporary, beginning in April 2027.

This two-year fellowship offers an early-career curator the opportunity to develop practical curatorial experience within a key contemporary art institution. Together, Asymmetry and Nottingham Contemporary have conceived the fellowship as a meaningful pathway into curatorial practice, combining hands-on institutional experience with space for independent research, experimentation and public engagement.

Embedded within Nottingham Contemporary’s curatorial team, the fellow will contribute to exhibitions, artist commissions, live programmes, research, writing, and institutional development, gaining experience across every stage of a project – from research and conception through production, public presentation and evaluation. A distinctive aspect of the fellowship is the opportunity to help shape new strands of Nottingham Contemporary’s live programme. Throughout the fellowship, the fellow will also be encouraged to develop and present their own research through Asymmetry’s programmes.

The Fellowship is open to an early-career curator with knowledge and experience of contemporary art, curatorial practices, and cultural ecosystems and who, to any extent, identifies with Chinese or Sinophone cultures or backgrounds.

The Fellowship offers an annual salary of 27,556 GBP (plus pension and National Insurance contributions), annual leave in line with the organisation’s leave policy in addition to UK bank holidays, and a package of support that includes visa and legal fee assistance where required, as well as a travel and relocation allowance.

Deadline: 25 October 2026

More info and apply: https://www.asymmetryart.org/fellowships/open-calls/2027-asymmetry-assistant-cu…

item.title: [News] European Commission: Artist-in-Residence 2027 on ‘Decoding Depression’ (Italy)
item.description:
Depression is one of the most widespread and complex mental health challenges in Europe today. It affects people across all ages, backgrounds and places, yet it is not experienced in the same way by everyone. Depression emerges through the entanglement of biological, psychological, social, cultural and environmental factors, and it is shaped by the conditions in which people live, work, move, connect and imagine their futures.

This residency invites artists to engage with depression not only as an individual condition, but also as a societal phenomenon shaped by multiple environments. In particular, applicants are encouraged to explore the environment as a creative and analytical lens: a framework that considers how interrelated personal, social, natural, built and digital environments influence health and wellbeing across the life course.

The selected artist will work in dialogue with researchers, policymakers and experts connected to the Digital Health Unit and the EU Policy Lab. This exchange may include access to selected background materials, discussions around current evidence on depression and environmental determinants of mental health, and opportunities to reflect on how artistic practice can engage with policy questions without being instrumentalised by them.

The residency is intended as a space for experimentation. Artists are encouraged to develop their own approach to the topic, whether through research-led, participatory, speculative, site-responsive, narrative, performative, digital or material practices.

The residency will take place at the Joint Research Centre in Ispra (Italy), with the possibility of a visit in Brussels. Artists will be working with an interdisciplinary team of scientists.

Artists are required to be present in Ispra for a minimum of 20 days across the six months (January to June 2027), spread as suits the work. The budget is 15,000 EUR in total, covering fees, allowance, accommodation and travel.

Deadline: 18 October 2026

More info and apply: https://knowledge4policy.ec.europa.eu/open-call-artist-residence-decoding-depre…

item.title: [News] The Supporting Act Foundation: 2027 Grants for Underrepresented Artists and Organisations
item.description:
The Supporting Act Foundation is as committed as ever to its mission of creating opportunities for underrepresented voices in the arts, working to empower emerging artists and arts-focused nonprofits and enabling them to meet their creative potential.

There are two streams:

  • 10 Impact Grants of 50,000 EUR, awarded over two years, to support arts-focused nonprofits
  • 10 Artist Grants of 10,000 EUR for emerging artists from underrepresented communities

Beyond funding, grantees join the Grantee Network, with access to online events and workshops, peer exchange, and promotion across our communication channels.

The Grants are for those based in Belgium, Germany, Spain, France, Greece, Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands, Portugal or the United Kingdom (or working with a fiscal host in one of these countries in the case of the Impact Grant).

Artists must self-identify as an emerging artist and be in the early stages of their career, with 2 to 10 years of professional experience actively pursuing artistic work as the main focus of their career.

Applicants must identify as belonging to one or more groups that are underrepresented or face systemic barriers in their country’s creative and cultural industries.

Deadline: 1 October 2026

More info and apply: https://thesupportingact.org/programs

item.title: [News] Nordic Culture Fund: ENTER Programme for Collaboration with a Nordic Focus
item.description:
ENTER is the Nordic Culture Fund’s programme for ambitious ideas which, in collaboration with others, can open up new perspectives and set new things in motion. The programme aims to offer space to experiment, learn as you go along and to test new directions, without necessarily knowing the concrete outcome.

ENTER stems from the ambition to bring arts and culture into play as a driving force that opens new perspectives, challenges established ways of thinking and contributes to shaping the future of the Nordic region. ENTER therefore offers the opportunity to explore an idea, method or way of working before its form, outcome or next step is entirely clear.

The Nordic Culture Fund is looking for initiatives that can apply and bring together different experiences, geographies and practices, and which have the courage to challenge established ways of working.

The initiative must have a Nordic anchoring and be built on collaboration across borders. Applications can only be for activities that take place after the funding decision from the Nordic Culture Fund has been received. The initiative must be completed and reported on no later than one year after the stated start date.

Both individuals and organisations can apply. Participants from outside the Nordic region can take part; what matters is not where participants come from or are based, but whether the initiative has a clear and meaningful relationship to the Nordic region.

Applicants can apply for up to 50 000 DKK, and there is no requirement for co-funding. The grant can be used for relevant costs related to delivering the initiative, including travel.

Deadline: 16 October 2026

More info and apply: https://nordiskkulturfond.org/en/funding-programmes/give-ambitious-ideas-space-…

item.title: [News] Cultivamos Cultura: ‘Bom Dia’ OASis Residency 2027 (Portugal)
item.description:
Cultivamos Cultura invites artists, designers, researchers and interdisciplinary creators to apply for Bom Dia OASis Residency.

OASis Bom Dia Residency (2027) is a site-responsive and community-oriented residency in São Luís, Portugal, exploring connections between artistic practice, ecology, local communities and sustainable futures.

The residency is looking for original, feasible and socially engaged projects across disciplines, particularly proposals working with local and/or natural materials, ecological themes, community engagement and collaborative practices.

Selected resident(s) will take part in a residency at Cultivamos Cultura and develop an artistic output to be presented to the local community and included in the OASis group exhibition in 2027.

This call is open to international creators / artists / researchers from various fields and disciplines, as well as practitioners and experts that operate at the intersection of culture and other disciplines. Applicants must state clearly on their application whether they are applying as a group or an individual. Groups may not exceed two persons with the understanding that the conditions and funding remain the same for a pair as for one individual.

The team of Cultivamos Cultura will provide occasional support to the project, but it is expected that the selected resident(s) is (are) reasonably autonomous in executing and producing all phases of the project, which will be evaluated based on their portfolio from recent years.

This residency includes:

  • A limited budget for travel of up to 500 EUR
  • Accommodation and a shared kitchen
  • A project fee of 1,300 EUR
  • Equitable per diem for food
  • Production/material expenses up to a maximum of 1,600 EUR
  • Free access to all spaces and resources of Cultivamos Cultura
  • Access to a workspace/studio

The call may close earlier if 100 applications are received.

Deadline: 30 October 2026

More info and apply: https://cultivamoscultura.com/2026/09/17/bom-dia-oasis-residency-call-for-2027/

item.title: [News] Salzburg Global: Cultural Futures Forum 2027 on Recognition, Equity, and Workforce Futures (Austria)
item.description:
The forces transforming work are reshaping a cultural and creative sector in which livelihoods have long been precarious. This Cultural Futures Forum will explore this topic online and in March 2027 in Salzburg, Austria.

Artificial intelligence, automation and digital platforms are transforming how culture is created, distributed and valued. New generations are entering the workforce, particularly in regions with rapidly growing young populations. Expectations around work, mobility, wellbeing and professional purpose are shifting, while creative production is becoming faster, more accessible and more abundant. These changes bring enormous possibility—but their benefits will not be shared equally. As the world of work is transformed, the central question is not only what will happen to creative work, but who will have the power, security and opportunity to build a creative life.

Programmes at Salzburg Global are co-designed with participants who work together to determine the program agenda. Participants should be available for the following dates:

  • Co-Creation Meeting 1 (Online): 4 February 2027
  • Co-Creation Meeting 2 (Online): 18 February 2027
  • In-Person Program (Salzburg, Austria): 14–19 March 2027

The programme is for: The people creating, imagining, questioning and experimenting; the organisations that preserve, commission, present and connect culture with audiences and communities; the businesses, technologies and sources of capital shaping how culture is financed, distributed and valued; the public institutions and leaders shaping the policies, investment and civic environments in which culture operates; and the institutions and thinkers bringing evidence, analysis and wider societal perspectives to the future of culture.

A limited number of scholarships to cover participation costs and travel will be available to individuals selected through the open call for participants. Scholarships will prioritise applicants from across the Majority World, as well as individuals and communities historically underrepresented in the arts and cultural sector. Partial scholarships are also available to support only participation costs or travel.

Deadline: 19 October 2026

More info and apply: https://www.salzburgglobal.org/topics/culture/culture-arts-and-society/session/…

item.title: [News] Goyki 3 Art Inkubator: 2027 Residency in Visual Art and Literature (Poland)
item.description:
Goyki 3 Art Inkubator in Sopot, Poland, invites contemporary visual artists and literature professionals for a two-month residency (taking place either in Spring or Autumn 2027).

Goyki 3 AiR focuses on supporting the creative process and dialogue between artists from various disciplines. By offering space and time for residents, the goal is to support the development of new projects or the continuation of existing ones. Goyki 3 does not prescribe the final outcome of the residency, nor do they impose a specific topic. Instead they support thoughtful, research-based projects that take into account their location: the city of Sopot and the Goyki 3 Art Inkubator space.

The 2027 residencies will take place on:

  • 5 April – 5 June (spring residence)
  • 13 September – 13 November (autumn residency)

Artistic duos may apply for the programme; their residency will be subject to the same conditions as for individual applications.

As part of the artistic residency, Art Inkubator provides residents with the following:

  • For the Spring Residency: Free accommodation in Sopot and a dedicated project budget of 2,000 PLN gross per resident. (Please note: travel costs are not covered).
  • For the Autumn Residency: A residency fee/stipend of up to 10,000 PLN gross per resident to cover accommodation and living expenses, plus a dedicated project budget of 2,000 PLN gross per resident. (Travel costs are not covered separately, but the stipend can be used to offset them).
  • For all residents: A dedicated studio workspace at the Art Inkubator and professional curatorial support.
Deadline: 14 October 2026

More info and apply: https://goyki3.pl/regulaminy/

item.title: [News] Ortaklaşa: EU-Türkiye Cultural Partnership Programme
item.description:
The Ortaklaşa EU-Türkiye Cultural Partnership Call for Proposals under the Ortaklaşa: Culture, Dialogue and Support Programme is open. The call will help foster arts- and culture-based cooperation networks among cities in Türkiye and Europe.

The Ortaklaşa EU-Türkiye Cultural Partnership Call for Proposals will bring together the local knowledge and experience of arts and culture organisations and municipalities in Türkiye and Europe through equal partnerships. The aim is for these collaborations to move beyond one-off project partnerships and develop into lasting relationships grounded in mutual learning, co-production and shared responsibility.

Projects supported under the Ortaklaşa EU-Türkiye Cultural Partnership Call are expected to strengthen the local cultural ecosystem in Türkiye while establishing lasting ties between cultural actors in Türkiye and Europe and creating a field of fair and sustainable cultural cooperation.

The project duration will be 9–12 months and it must be implemented primarily in Türkiye. Activities can include:

  • Activities with Impact on Policy-Making Processes in Arts and Culture
  • Artistic Production and Participatory Cultural Events
  • Capacity Building and Experience Sharing Activities
  • Infrastructure and Organisational Strengthening
  • Outreach, Visibility and Communication Activities

Within the scope of this call, applications are expected to be submitted through a four-institution cooperation structure consisting of:

  • A culture-oriented CSO based in Türkiye as the lead applicant,
  • A culture-oriented CSO based in an EU member state or candidate country (Albania, Iceland, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Kosovo or Serbia) as the partner,
  • One municipality from Türkiye as associates, and
  • One municipality from an EU member state or candidate country (Albania, Iceland, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Kosovo or Serbia) as associates.

The grant amount per project is between 60,000 EUR and 120,000 EUR. Grant support may cover between 70% and 95% of the projects’ total eligible costs.

Deadline: 18 December 2026

More info and apply: https://ortaklasa.iksv.org/en/ortaklasa-culture-dialogue-and-support-programme/

item.title: [News] dot.ateliers: 2027 Artist Residency (Ghana)
item.description:
dot.ateliers | south labadi, an initiative founded by artist Amoako Boafo, has an open call for artists to participate in the 2027 Artist Residency Programme. This opportunity invites mark makers to immerse themselves in an inspiring and supportive environment in the heart of Accra, Ghana.

The dot.ateliers residency programme is designed to foster creativity, collaboration, and exploration, providing artists with the space and resources they need to deepen their artistic practices. The serene and captivating location in Accra’s city center offers a transformative experience for emerging and established artists alike.

The residency runs for a minimum of 6 weeks and up to 3 months, depending on availability and the artist’s proposal.

Artists over 18 of all backgrounds, genders, and nationalities are encouraged to apply. Applicants should demonstrate a commitment to pushing their creative boundaries and engaging with the residency community.

The resident receives a material stipend, and 24-hour access to the studio space and accommodation. The residency also covers the artists’ travel expense to Accra.

Deadline: 12 October 2026

More info and apply: https://www.dotateliers.space/apply

item.title: [News] Festival ADAR: Residency for Groups Based in Europe 2026–2027 (Spain)
item.description:
Festival ADAR are looking for groups of 4–5 artists/cultural professionals, legally residing outside Spain, for a 21- to 30-day residency in rural Asturias, Spain, to take place before 7 June 2027.

This is a space for A space for research, creation, experimentation, rehearsal, artistic development, preparation of a future work, recording, exhibition or performance. A finished work is not required. The proposal can be simple, and it can be one stage of a larger project you will complete later.

The residency takes place in Leiguarda, a small village in Belmonte de Miranda, surrounded by the mountains and landscape of central Asturias.

Eligible sectors include: architecture, cultural heritage, design and fashion design, literature, music, performing arts, and visual arts.

Each artist receives:

  • 30 EUR/day
  • 400 EUR–800 EUR travel support
  • accommodation
  • additional top-ups available when applicable
Deadline: 28 September 2026

More info and apply: https://festivaladar.com/en/artist-residency-open-call-2026-27/
